 1                        I.   WITNESS IDENTIFICATION

 2   Q.   Please state your name and business address.

 3   A.   My name is Taylor J. Hurt. My business address is 790 South Buchanan Street,

 4        Amarillo, Texas 79101.

 5   Q.   On whose behalf are you testifying in this proceeding?

 6   A.   I am filing testimony on behalf of Southwestern Public Service Company (“SPS”),

 7        a New Mexico corporation and a wholly-owned subsidiary of Xcel Energy Inc.

 8   Q.   Are you the same Taylor J. Hurt who filed direct testimony on behalf of SPS

 9        in this case?

10   A.   Yes.




                                              1
                                   Case No. 25-00079-UT

                                            of
                                       Taylor J. Hurt

 1                II.    PURPOSE AND SUMMARY OF TESTIMONY

 2   Q.   What is the purpose of your testimony in this phase of the case?

 3   A.   I am providing testimony in support of the Comprehensive Stipulation

 4        (“Stipulation”), particularly Section 1.3 – Cunningham Battery Energy Storage

 5        System (“BESS”) Direct Assignment; Section 1.11 – Revenue Allocation and Rate

 6        Design; 1.12 – Electric Affordability Program (“EAP”); and 1.17 – Jurisdictional

 7        Allocation Adjustment. Specifically, my testimony will:

 8           •   discuss that SPS should be authorized to assign all costs and capacity
 9               benefits of the Cunningham BESS to SPS’s New Mexico retail customers;

10           •   support the allocation of the Hale and Sagamore wind facilities on an
11               average and excess demand four-coincident peak (“AED-4CP”) basis;

12           •   support the use of a one coincident peak (“1CP”) system load factor used in
13               the AED-4CP calculation;

14           •   acknowledge SPS’s commitment to study behind-the-meter (“BTM”)
15               impacts to jurisdictional and customer class cost of service;

16           •   support SPS’s EAP program and tariff; and

17           •   support the calculations and methodology to remove load served by the
18               direct assigned Cunningham BESS in the 12-coincident-peak (“12-CP”)
19               allocator used to allocate costs of shared system production resources.




                                              2
                                    Case No. 25-00079-UT
                                   Testimony in Support of
                                  Comprehensive Stipulation
                                             of
                                        Taylor J. Hurt

 1             III.    DIRECT ASSIGNMENT OF CUNNINGHAM BESS

 2   Q.   Does SPS support and agree to implement Section 1.3 of the Stipulation?

 3   A.   Yes. SPS supports and agrees to implement Section 1.3 of the Stipulation, which

 4        provides that the Cunningham BESS is directly assigned to New Mexico retail

 5        customers, including both the associated costs and accredited capacity benefits.

 6   Q.   How has SPS reflected the requirements of Section 1.3?

 7   A.   SPS has reflected the direct assignment of the Cunningham BESS in its

 8        jurisdictional cost of service by ensuring that the costs of the resource and its

 9        accredited capacity are assigned to New Mexico retail customers, consistent with

10        the Stipulation.

11               Under the agreed methodology, SPS will calculate the net accredited

12        capacity benefit by adjusting the seasonal Cunningham BESS accredited capacity

13        for the applicable seasonal planning reserve margin (“PRM”). For the summer

14        period, May through October, the Cunningham BESS accredited capacity value

15        assigned to New Mexico will equal the summer Cunningham BESS accredited

16        capacity divided by one plus the applicable summer PRM. For the winter period,

17        November through April, the Cunningham BESS accredited capacity value


                                               3
                                   Case No. 25-00079-UT
                                  Testimony in Support of
                                 Comprehensive Stipulation
                                            of
                                       Taylor J. Hurt

 1        assigned to New Mexico will equal the winter Cunningham BESS accredited

 2        capacity divided by one plus the applicable winter PRM.

 3   Q.   Why is it reasonable to assign both Cunningham BESS costs and capacity

 4        benefits to New Mexico retail customers?

 5   A.   Several parties, including NMLCG and Staff, submitted testimony in support of the

 6        position that if New Mexico retail customers are assigned the costs of Cunningham

 7        BESS, they should also receive the capacity benefit associated with that resource.

 8        As part of the negotiated resolution and compromise included in the Stipulation,

 9        SPS agreed to credit New Mexico customers with the system capacity benefit

10        provided by the Cunningham BESS.

11   Q.   How does the Stipulation reflect the Cunningham BESS capacity benefit in

12        jurisdictional allocation?

13   A.   Section 1.17 explains the allocation mechanism in detail. SPS will adjust the 12-

14        CP production jurisdictional system allocator to remove the New Mexico load

15        served by the accredited capacity of the Cunningham BESS from the shared system

16        capacity pool used to allocate shared system production resources.

17               Stated more simply, the 12-CP allocator divides shared system production

18        costs between New Mexico and Texas based on each jurisdiction’s demand during


                                              4
                                    Case No. 25-00079-UT
                                   Testimony in Support of
                                  Comprehensive Stipulation
                                             of
                                        Taylor J. Hurt

 1        SPS’s monthly system peaks. Because the Stipulation assigns Cunningham BESS

 2        to New Mexico, it also treats part of New Mexico’s peak demand as being served

 3        by Cunningham BESS rather than by shared system production resources. SPS

 4        therefore reduces the New Mexico load included in the 12-CP allocator by the

 5        agreed capacity value of Cunningham BESS.

 6               That adjustment lowers the amount of shared system production capacity

 7        allocated to New Mexico compared to a calculation that ignored the Cunningham

 8        BESS capacity benefit. In practical terms, New Mexico customers are assigned the

 9        costs of Cunningham BESS, and the 12-CP allocator is adjusted so that New

10        Mexico is not also allocated shared system production capacity for the portion of

11        New Mexico load treated as served by Cunningham BESS.

12   Q.   Please explain how the accredited capacity of the Cunningham BESS is

13        reflected in the jurisdictional allocation.

14   A.   The accredited capacity is reflected through an adjustment to the 12-CP Production

15        Jurisdictional allocator by reducing New Mexico’s coincident peak load for the

16        portion of capacity that is directly attributable to the Cunningham BESS. This

17        reflects that the resource serves New Mexico retail customers and reduces their

18        reliance on shared system capacity.

                                                5
                                    Case No. 25-00079-UT
                                   Testimony in Support of
                                  Comprehensive Stipulation
                                             of
                                        Taylor J. Hurt

1    Q.   How does that adjustment account for planning reserve margin requirements?

2    A.   The adjustment is limited to the portion of the accredited capacity that is available

3         to serve load. A portion of the accredited capacity must be reserved to satisfy

4         Southwest Power Pool planning reserve margin requirements, which are held above

 5        peak load. Because the 12-CP allocator measures load responsibility at system

 6        peak, only the load-serving portion of the accredited capacity is used to reduce New

 7        Mexico’s coincident peak. This approach ensures that the jurisdictional allocator

 8        reflects how the resource actually reduces load responsibility, while avoiding

 9        double counting of capacity that is simultaneously used to satisfy reserve

10        requirements and more accurately captures New Mexico’s use of shared production

11        resources.

12   Q.   Have you prepared an attachment to show how this adjustment is applied?

13   A.   Yes. Attachment TJH-STIP-1 shows the adjusted production jurisdictional

14        allocator.

1   Q.   Does Section 1.3 require any additional actions beyond the direct assignment

2        itself?

3   A.   Yes. Section 1.3 also contemplates further evaluation of jurisdictional allocation

4        principles as they relate to directly assigned resources. SPS agrees to participate in

5        this stakeholder process and to evaluate how divergent state resource portfolios

6        should be reflected in jurisdictional allocation methodologies.

 1            IV.    REVENUE ALLOCATION AND RATE DESIGN

 2   Q.   Does SPS support and agree to implement the provisions in Section 1.11 of

 3        the Stipulation?

 4   A.   Yes. SPS supports and agrees to implement the provisions in Section 1.11 of the

 5        Stipulation and has reflected those requirements in its class cost of service study.

 6   Q.   How did you treat Hale and Sagamore in your class cost of service study?

 7   A.   Consistent with the Stipulation, the costs of the Hale and Sagamore resources are

 8        allocated using the AED-4CP methodology. Specifically, Hale and Sagamore costs

 9        have been moved out of the Energy functional component and into Production

10        Demand and Transmission Interconnect components, which are allocated to each

11        customer class on an AED-4CP basis.

12   Q.   How did you calculate the system load factor used in the AED-4CP

13        methodology for purposes of the Stipulation?

14   A.   For purposes of implementing the Stipulation, the system load factor has been

15        calculated using a 1-CP approach, consistent with the agreement of the settling

16        parties. This 1-CP system load factor was used as an input to the AED-4CP

17        production and transmission allocators.




                                                8
                                     Case No. 25-00079-UT
                                    Testimony in Support of
                                   Comprehensive Stipulation
                                              of
                                         Taylor J. Hurt

1    Q.   Does Section 1.11 require any additional analysis related to behind-the-meter

2         generation?

3    A.   Yes. Section 1.11 requires SPS to evaluate the impact of adjustments to the

4         transmission allocators to account for behind-the-meter generation. SPS agrees to

5         complete the required study and evaluation of behind-the-meter generation impacts

6         and report on the results of the study in its next base rate case.

7    Q.   Have you prepared a class cost of service study that reflects all of these

8         changes?

9    A.   Yes. Attachment TJH-STIP-2 is the class cost of service study which reflects the

10        use of a 1-CP system load factor used in the AED-4CP calculations and the

11        allocation of Hale and Sagamore on an AED-4CP basis.

 1              V.      ELECTRIC AFFORDABILITY PROGRAM

 2   Q.   Has SPS completed, or will it complete, the specific commitments identified in

 3        Section 1.12 of the Stipulation?

 4   A.   Yes. SPS has completed, or will complete, all required actions set forth in Section

 5        1.12 of the Stipulation, including updating its affordability analysis, coordinating

 6        program implementation, and convening a collaborative working group within the

 7        required timeframe. SPS will coordinate EAP implementation with other low-

 8        income programs, including energy efficiency, weatherization, LIHEAP, and

 9        customer outreach resources. SPS will also provide the required reporting and

10        evaluation of the program in its next base rate case.

                                    Case No. 25-00079-UT
                                   Testimony in Support of
                                  Comprehensive Stipulation
                                             of
                                        Taylor J. Hurt

 1          VI.     JURISDICTIONAL ALLOCATION ADJUSTMENT

 2   Q.   Does SPS support and agree to implement the jurisdictional allocation

 3        provisions in Section 1.17 of the Stipulation?

 4   A.   Yes. SPS supports and agrees to implement the provisions in Section 1.17.

 5   Q.   Has SPS implemented the required adjustments?

 6   A.   Yes. As discussed in Section III of this testimony, the required adjustments to SPS’s

 7        production jurisdictional allocation methodology to reflect the direct assignment of

8         the Cunningham BESS have been implemented in the cost of service, consistent

 9        with the Stipulation. This adjustment is displayed in Attachment TJH-STIP-1.

10   Q.   Does this conclude pre-filed testimony in support of the Stipulation?

11   A.   Yes.
